title: Continuous Data Curation and Valuation for Long-Term Machine Learning Model Health: A Comprehensive Review
venue: European Journal of Science and Modern Technologies
tldr: The DataSphere framework for autonomous data lifecycle management addresses ML model degradation through integrated curation, valuation, and drift detection, though practical implementation challenges remain.
problem_and_motivation: ML models experience 'AI ageing' - gradual performance degradation due to data drift, quality erosion, and changing distributions. Current ML systems lack integrated data-centric approaches, treating data work as manual janitorial tasks rather than first-class citizens of the ML lifecycle. The static-world assumption leads to brittle pipelines where data quality issues are discovered late.
approach: Comprehensive review proposing DataSphere framework integrating automated curation, data valuation (Shapley values, influence functions, gradient similarity), drift detection (DDM, ADWIN, Page-Hinkley, K-S statistic, PSI), and active learning (uncertainty sampling, diversity sampling, RL-based). Formalizes model health as H(t) = f(A(t), R(t), F(t), D(t)) incorporating accuracy, robustness, fairness, and distributional drift. Provides taxonomy of curation tasks (data integrity vs data relevance) and implementation roadmap.
findings: The review demonstrates that continuous data curation can maintain model performance near peak levels ('sawtooth' pattern) compared to natural decay. Data Shapley provides theoretically rigorous valuation but is NP-hard; influence functions enable efficient debugging but assume convex loss; gradient similarity scales well but lacks theoretical guarantees. The feedback loop between drift detection, curation, and valuation creates self-adapting systems. Active learning can achieve target performance with 50% less labeled data.

definitions.AI ageing: Gradual decline in ML model performance over time due to data drift and quality erosion
definitions.Concept drift: Change in the relationship between input variables and target variable P(y|X)
definitions.Covariate drift: Change in the distribution of input variables P(X)
definitions.Data Shapley: Cooperative game theory approach for equitable valuation of data points' contribution to model performance
definitions.Influence functions: Robust statistics method estimating impact of training observations on model parameters
definitions.DataSphere: Proposed unified framework for autonomous data lifecycle management integrating curation, valuation, drift detection, and active learning

limitations: Comprehensive review but lacks empirical validation of proposed DataSphere framework
Shapley value computation remains NP-hard, limiting practical application
Assumes convex loss for influence functions, unstable for deep learning
Active learning limited to unlabelled data; value depends on query strategy
Practical implementation requires significant engineering effort and integration complexity
remember_this: ML models suffer from 'AI ageing' due to data drift and quality erosion. The proposed DataSphere framework integrates continuous curation, data valuation, and drift detection into self-adapting systems. Active learning can reduce labeling costs by 50% while maintaining performance. The shift from model-centric to data-centric AI is essential for sustainable ML systems.
